evals.name: set-up-an-isolated-branch
evals.prompt:
I'm about to start ticket HAR-421 on this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there) — a multi-commit change to the promotion step. Several other agents are working this repo at the same time.

Set me up. Give me the exact commands for this repo and tell me what to report back. Save it as setup.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The setup creates a new branch in its own git worktree, not a branch in the shared checkout
It fetches first and branches off the integration branch named in harness.yaml, naming the branch this repo actually declares, rather than off whatever the local checkout last saw
It creates the worktree detached and runs the repo's declared verify command in it before the branch is cut, rather than assuming the base is green
It states what a red base means — an andon pull: file the failure as a bug against the integration branch, remove the worktree, hold the task, and do not repair the base inside this ticket's tree
It symlinks the gitignored local state from the shared root, anchoring the path to the shared root computed from git rather than to the current directory
The branch name identifies the task
It requires reporting which commit the work started from and the result of the base gate run

evals.name: cleanup-after-merge
evals.prompt:
HAR-421 on this repository merged. During the task I started a local dev server on port 8081 and built a Docker Compose project for the worktree. There are two other worktrees on this host for other tickets, and a stash somebody left.

Clean up. Save the sequence as cleanup.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: Task-owned services are stopped before their files are removed
Cleanup removes the worktree, prunes git's administrative records, and deletes the merged branch
It only removes resources this task created, named by the identifiers retained when they were provisioned
It explicitly does not run a broad host-wide cleanup, and does not touch the other worktrees
It does not drop the stash somebody else left without confirming first
It says uncommitted work in the worktree is lost when the worktree is removed, so commit or discard first

evals.name: parallel-sub-agents
evals.prompt:
I'm orchestrating a change on this repository and I want to fan three implementation sub-agents out across three modules at once, then review the combined result myself.

Is that safe? Tell me how to set it up, or what to do instead. Save it as parallel.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer requires each concurrently-running agent to have its own worktree
It states the reason: two agents editing the same working tree corrupt each other's diffs
It says a single sub-agent may share the orchestrator's worktree only while the orchestrator is idle
It gives the concrete setup — one worktree per agent, each on its own branch
It says how the three results are brought back together

evals.name: a-task-this-host-may-already-hold
evals.prompt:
I want to start ticket HAR-512 on this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). It is sitting in Todo and nobody is assigned.

Before you do anything: `git worktree list` on this host shows `/Users/me/Code/harness` on the integration branch, `/Users/me/Code/harness-51` on branch `51-token-audit`, and `/Users/me/Code/harness-512` on branch `512-retry-budget`. I don't know who made the last one or whether anything is running in it.

Walk me through the setup for HAR-512, in order, and tell me what you would report. Save it as setup.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: It asks whether another worktree or branch on this host already carries HAR-512, and asks it before the ticket is transitioned, assigned, or commented on — not after, and not as part of cutting the worktree
It identifies `/Users/me/Code/harness-512` on `512-retry-budget` as carrying this task
It does not treat `/Users/me/Code/harness-51` on `51-token-audit` as carrying HAR-512, matching the task as a delimited segment rather than as a substring
On the match it stops and reports — naming the path, the branch, and what that worktree's run state last recorded — rather than removing the directory, reusing it, or proceeding to cut a second one
It does not decide from a timestamp or an age whether the other run is still alive, and does not wait for it to expire
It says the directory is recoverable by the operator: where it turns out to be their own ended run, the work is resumed from it rather than abandoned
It writes nothing to the tracker on the stop

evals.name: a-red-base-somebody-is-already-repairing
evals.prompt:
I'm starting ticket HAR-530 on this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I cut the detached worktree and ran the repo's verify command in it. It failed: `tests/unit/test_promotion_step_script.py::test_the_gate_runs_inside_the_checkout` errors, and nothing I have done could have caused it — I have changed no files.

The repo's open queue has one P1 bug, `HAR-528`, titled "Promotion step loses the checkout path". Its most recent comment is a run saying it took the repair, timestamped 20 minutes ago. `harness.yaml` declares `loop.cord_claim_minutes: 120`.

What do I do? Give me the sequence and what to report. Save it as redbase.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: It treats the red base as an andon pull and does not cut the branch or build on it
Before anything is filed, it searches the open queue keyed to the failure — the failing test or the surface it names — rather than to the wording of a title
It identifies HAR-528 as covering this failure and files no new bug, adding the evidence to HAR-528 instead
It reads the 20-minute-old comment against the declared 120-minute bound and concludes the repair is in flight
It still holds HAR-530 and stops: a repair in flight does not license building on the red base, and does not leave HAR-530 sitting In Progress
The report names HAR-528 and how old its claim is, so the operator can see what would clear the base
It says that with no such open P1, or with a claim older than the declared bound, the outcome is unchanged — file the bug or extend the existing one, remove the worktree, hold the task, and stop
It does not repair HAR-528's defect inside HAR-530's tree
